changes.comment: BREAKING: Review: Feishu COT cards are now keyed by recipient rather than by Feishu target. Every TeamLeader and the Dispatcher owns exactly one standing anchor and at most one open card, wherever the anchor came from. A Feishu inbound becomes that anchor only after Core reports that steering or queueing it succeeded; on that success the open card closes and its successor opens under the new message, without waiting for logical settlement or a native turn end, while a rejected, failed, or ambiguous admission changes nothing. Facts Core publishes synchronously inside the admitting call are best effort: such a body or early activity may still land on the predecessor card, or produce no card when no anchor exists yet. A card now closes only when the runtime reports the end of its one native turn (completed closes as done; failed or interrupted closes as interrupted); that fact closes an already open card and never opens one, so it is ignored when no card is open. `teammate.turn.settled` no longer closes, reopens, or re-anchors anything. A card create or append the platform refuses abandons only that card: the standing anchor survives, and the next opening activity tries to open a card there again. A Reply is outbound only and never creates, replaces, or retires an anchor. Once a recipient has an anchor, every projected input is shown, including the user body this Channel submitted, task, task-notification, cron, system, and future source names. The Channel keeps no per-turn body-suppression ledger, cap, or one-shot mark. A visible Team bind card may initialize a TeamLeader that has no standing anchor and never replaces an existing one; the Dispatcher has no installation or restart anchor. A tool result that arrives after an anchor replacement may be omitted. Anchors and cards live only in the live session's memory and are lost on restart by design, with no replay or backfill. The package's public export surface is unchanged; the target-keyed and dispatcher-scoped COT presentation modules this replaces were always internal. No transport, configuration, persisted state, or path shape changed and no rebuild is required.
